predecessors.name: Buyid dynasty
predecessors.text: Hulwan, taken by Abu al-Fath Muhammad ibn Annaz in 991

predecessors.name: Hasanwayhids
predecessors.text: the Jibal lands of the Hasanwayhids after 1014-1015

successors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
successors.text: the Annazid lands, which the page leaves undated after 1055

ledger.x: 991: Abu al-Fath Muhammad ibn Annaz takes Hulwan.
1015: the Annazids replace the Hasanwayhids in the Jibal.
1040: Ala al-Dawla annexes Kermanshah and Dinavar.
1117: the Annazids are said to have collapsed by 1117.

wars.name: Annazid-Hasanwayhid struggle for the Jibal
wars.outcome: Badr expelled Abu al-Fath ibn Annaz; hostilities resumed in 1006-1007; Abu al-Fath recaptured Shahrizor in 1013 and the Annazids replaced the Hasanwayhids in the Jibal after Badr's death in 1014.

wars.name: Annazid-Kakuyid war over Kermanshah and Dinavar
wars.outcome: Ala al-Dawla annexed Kermanshah and Dinavar in 1040; Muhalhil recaptured them in 1047.

wars.name: Seljuk overrun of the Annazids
wars.outcome: Tughril sent Ibrahim Yinal west in 1045 and the Annazid lands were overrun; Turkomans defeated Sa'adi and took Sirwan in 1047; in 1050 Tughril reinstated the Annazids as vassals with Muhalhil in Sirwan.

certainty.note: A Kurdish emirate of fortress towns along the Zagros: Hulwan, Dinavar, Kermanshah, Shahrizor; no frontiers on the page.
